prompt_context.issue_body: ## Summary Implements `signMultiple` on `ArkadeRemoteIdentity`. Its mere presence flips the Arkade SDK onto its batch-signing branch (`isBatchSignable` = `"signMultiple" in identity`), so the arkTx and **every checkpoint are signed before `submitTx`** instead of between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`. That removes the interruption window where a dropped connection left a send half-finalized and stranded funds (input spent, output never a spendable VTXO). In the batch path the only work left between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx` is a local `combineTapscriptSigs` — no network, no passkey. `signMultiple` reuses the existing, in-production per-input sign path sequentially — **no new crypto/MuSig2-nonce code**. The session-scoped send approval already authorizes signing all checkpoints up front, and pre-existing partial sigs are preserved (clone + `tapScriptSig` merge-update). Verified against `@arkade-os/sdk` 0.4.38 (`buildAndSubmitOffchainTx`, `isBatchSignable`, `canBatch`). ### Scope: primary fix only This PR ships the **primary** fix. The **secondary** item from #768 — auto-run `finalizePendingTxs` on launch/foreground + replace the global `hasPendingTx` boolean with a per-tx record — is **split out / out of scope** here: - The primary fix already removes the strand window, so auto-recovery is now edge-case insurance, not the P0. - `finalizePendingTxs` signs via `identity.sign()`, which requires an armed approval scope and **prompts Face ID** when a tx is actually pending — it needs a designed recovery UX, not a silent foreground trigger. - The per-tx-record change lives in the vendored `@arkade-os/sdk` and belongs upstream. Interim manual recovery: the debug section can trigger `finalizePendingTxs`. prompt_context.issue_title: #768: Interrupted Arkade send strands funds: serialized MuSig2 signing between submitTx and finalizeTx

linked_issues.body: ## Summary A connection drop during an outgoing Arkade Lightning send can strand funds: the input VTXO is marked spent (pending) but the send never finalizes, so the output never becomes a spendable VTXO. Balance drops to 0, nothing shows in pending, and recovery needs the operator to re-serve the pending tx. Root cause: our `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` signs checkpoints one-at-a-time (serialized MuSig2 round-trips) *between* `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`, creating a long window where a dropped connection leaves the tx half-finalized. ## Why / Reasoning **Incident (mainnet, release/v0.87.0):** bought BTC → arrived on Arkade boarding → paid a ~28.6k-sat Lightning invoice → confirmed with passkey → balance dropped to 0, money didn't arrive, no pending tx shown. ~72.5k sats stranded. **Trace (verified against `arkade.computer` indexer + Boltz):** - Input VTXO `0bf0f1d7…:0` (72,501): `isSpent=true`, `spentBy=fe6793a3…`, still returned under `pendingOnly=true`. - Spending ark tx `e0726e…` was **submitted but never finalized**. Its output checkpoint `46c2ea…` was never indexed as a spendable VTXO (`/vtxos?outpoints=fe6793a3…:0` → `[]`). - The tx had **16 inputs → 16 checkpoints**. **Root cause — signing architecture:** - `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` is a MuSig2 2-of-2 (client + `arkade.nuri.com` server), client key unlocked via WebAuthn passkey PRF. Every signature is an interactive MuSig2 nonce round-trip. - It does **not** implement `signMultiple`, so the SDK's `isBatchSignable()` is false and the batch fast-path is skipped. - On the non-batch path the SDK signs the arkTx before `submitTx`, then signs each checkpoint **after** `submitTx` via `Promise.all(checkpoints.map(sign))`. Our `signingKeyVault.runSignExclusive` (single-flight `signOpTail` queue) then **serializes** those. So 16 checkpoints = 16 sequential MuSig2 round-trips sitting between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`. - The connection dropped in that window → `finalizeTx` never ran → half-finalized checkpoint. **Secondary finding — no client self-recovery:** - The app never auto-runs `finalizePendingTxs` (only our new debug button does). - `finalizePendingTxs` short-circuits on a single **global** `hasPendingTx` boolean; a later successful send clears it, erasing the "interrupted send" marker. So even the SDK's designed recovery never fires. **Recovery performed (proves the diagnosis):** Arkade re-served the pending tx on `/v1/tx/pending`; we finalized client-side (intent built over the spent input + force-set the pending flag — debug tooling). 50,493 change returned immediately; 28,609 landed in the Boltz VHTLC (swap `FktQNozCtAY6`, invoice expired) → recoverable via the `refundWithoutReceiver` CLTV on 2026-07-13. ## Decisions - **Primary fix:** implement `signMultiple` on `ArkadeRemoteIdentity` (+ batched MuSig2 nonce exchange with the cosigner server). In the SDK batch path *all* signing (arkTx + every checkpoint) happens up front before `submitTx`; finalize only `combineTapscriptSigs`. Result: **zero client round-trips between `submitTx` and `finalizeTx`** → the interruption window is removed. - **Secondary:** auto-run `finalizePendingTxs` on launch/foreground, and replace the global `hasPendingTx` boolean with a per-tx pending record so a later send can't erase an unfinalized one. ## Trade-offs / Risks - MuSig2 batched nonce handling must be correct — no secret-nonce reuse across the batch. The current serialization exists partly for nonce safety + single-flight passkey; batching must preserve those invariants. - `_signerRouter.canBatch(...)` must also return true for the batch path to engage — verify our router reports batch capability. - Auto-running `finalizePendingTxs` at launch adds a signed `/v1/tx/pending` call (passkey scope) on startup when a pending marker exists — gate it so it only runs when needed. ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph now[Current — non-batch] A1[sign arkTx] --> A2[submitTx] --> A3[sign 16 checkpoints\nserialized MuSig2 round-trips] --> A4[finalizeTx]

prompt_context.issue_body: Follow-up review fixes for #758 that landed on `fix/086-ota-pwa-native` after it was merged to `dev`. Two commits. ## High 1. **Native passkey login now requires user verification.** `PasskeyLoginScreenWebView`'s create/get ceremonies used `userVerification: "preferred"`. Native iOS/Android now route login/restore through this WebView (the native module is dormant), so an assertion could be accepted without the user being biometrically verified — a downgrade from the native path. All three ceremonies are now `"required"`, matching `PasskeyWebAuthnPrfView`. ## Medium 2. **Android hardware-back no longer falls through Layer modals.** `LayerHost` let back propagate to the screen behind a top layer, so the forced-update / biometric-lock / passkey-confirm screens could be backed out of. A visible top layer now always consumes back (parity with the RN `<Modal>` it replaced), running `onRequestClose` when dismissible. Back now dismisses/cancels `PaymentReceivedModal` and the WebAuthn PRF overlay. 3. **Guard pending-send removal.** The arkade reconcile `remove()` is wrapped in try/catch so a storage failure can't surface as an unhandled rejection in the pending-send interval. <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved back-button and close behavior for layered screens and modals, so dismiss actions are handled more consistently. * Passkey PRF flows now use stricter verification settings, which may reduce unexpected authentication issues. * Closing the PRF overlay now properly cancels the active request and shows a clearer busy state when another request is already running. * Pending Bitcoin sends are now cleared more reliably even if a cleanup step fails. <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

prompt_context.issue_body: ## Summary - Enables hardware security keys (YubiKey, Titan, etc.) to work without requiring PIN setup - Maintains strong security for platform authenticators (Face ID, Touch ID) - Fixes timeout issues when iOS apps register hardware keys ## The Problem When the server required `userVerification: 'required'`, it caused two issues: 1. **User Experience**: iOS would prompt YubiKey users to set up a PIN, even if they just wanted touch-only authentication 2. **Technical Issue**: When iOS apps overrode this to `discouraged` to avoid the PIN prompt, the server would reject the registration with "User verification was required, but user could not be verified" This created a catch-22: either force users to set up PINs (poor UX) or registrations would fail (broken functionality). ## The Solution Changed two key settings: 1. **During Registration Options**: ```javascript authenticatorSelection: { residentKey: 'required', userVerification: 'preferred', // Changed from 'required' } ``` 2. **During Verification**: ```javascript requireUserVerification: false, // Changed from true ``` ## How It Works Now ### For Hardware Security Keys (YubiKey, etc.): - Server says "user verification preferred" (not required) - iOS can use `.discouraged` to avoid PIN prompts - User just touches the key - no PIN needed - Server accepts the registration ✅ ### For Platform Authenticators (Face ID, Touch ID): - Still use biometric verification - Security unchanged - Better user experience maintained ## Testing Tested with: - ✅ iOS app with YubiKey 5 NFC (touch-only, no PIN) - ✅ Web dashboard with platform authenticators - ✅ Existing registered credentials continue to work ## Security Considerations This change is safe because: 1. **Hardware keys** still require: - Physical possession of the key - User presence (touch) - Cryptographic proof of key ownership 2. **Platform authenticators** still require: - Biometric or device PIN verification - No security reduction 3. **Industry standard**: Major services (Google, GitHub, etc.) use the same approach ## Breaking Changes None. This change is backwards compatible: - Existing credentials continue to work - New registrations work with more authenticator types - Authentication flow unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added detailed documentation outlining the architecture and API for a passkey-based encryption key storage system, including security considerations and future enhancements. * **Refactor** * Relaxed user verification requirements during passkey registration and authentication to improve usability. * Corrected parameter naming in authentication verification for greater accuracy. <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

It takes feat/pwa-web's app wholesale (no native modals via `LayerHost`, the in-WebView one-tap passkey ceremony, held-key signing) and **pins the four fingerprint inputs back to 0.86.0's exact bytes** so the runtimeVersion fingerprint matches the submitted binary and `eas update --channel production` delivers it. Replaces #756 (which took the opposite, native-modal approach). Built on top of #748's branch. ## How it's constructed - Base = `feat/pwa-web` (the full PWA UX + held-key signing vault). - **Pinned to 0.86.0** (byte-identical, the only commit on top of the base): `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `app.config.ts`, `.gitignore`. This restores `expo-local-authentication ~16.0.5`, `react-native-svg ^15.12.1`, `minSdkVersion 30`, etc. — so the fingerprint matches the approved build. The PWA code doesn't import the restored deps (they sit present-but-unused for fingerprint parity), except secureKeyStorage below. - **#585 restored** via the pinned `lib/secureKeyStorage.ts`: weak-biometric Android keeps the `DEVICE_PASSCODE` floor (key unreadable without device auth). **iOS is unchanged from feat/pwa-web** — every #585 delta is `Platform.OS === "android"`-gated. feat/pwa-web's `BiometricLockModal` is kept (PWA rendering); it gates unlock by *reading* the now-#585-protected key, so the Android protection flows through `secureKeyStorage` — no separate lock-modal logic needed. ## Fingerprint gate (must pass before publish) The OTA only delivers if the bundle's fingerprint byte-matches the submitted 0.86.0 builds. Pinning the inputs should achieve this; confirm with `eas fingerprint:compare` against both production builds before `eas update`, exactly as #743 did. ## ⚠️ Security review required before production This routes the native passkey ceremony through an **in-WebView WebAuthn/PRF bridge** (`WebAuthnPrfService` + always-mounted `WebAuthnPrfOverlay`), with the native module left dormant. The WebView path handles passkey assertions, PRF, and key-material flows — it needs a security review before shipping to prod. ## Not included - SSE instant-incoming claim is **web-only** on feat/pwa-web; native stays on polling. That "no long pending on incoming" does not transfer to the native binary. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors - fingerprint inputs byte-match 0.86.0 (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `app.config.ts`, `.gitignore`, `lib/secureKeyStorage.ts`) <!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai --> ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added global in-app WebAuthn PRF/passkey overlays and improved passkey onboarding/unlock with prefilled ceremonies. * Enabled real-time Lightning incoming updates on web via server-sent events. * Improved web experience with PWA setup, manifest/icons, same-origin API proxying, and checkout opening in a new tab. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved number/amount alignment on web. * Reduced duplicate receive-sync requests. * Standardized overlay/sheet/modal stacking and dismissal across the app. * Prevented biometric/app-lock behavior issues on web and tightened key handling for lock/reset flows. <!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

linked_issues.body: ## Problem Two related enforcement gaps, verified in react-native-keychain 10.0.0 source: **1. Android silently stores wallet keys with no auth requirement when no strong biometrics exist.** `KeychainModule.kt` computes `useBiometry = getUseBiometry(accessControl) && (isFingerprintAuthAvailable || isFaceAuthAvailable || isIrisAuthAvailable)`. On devices without strong (Class 3) biometrics, auth-requiring cipher storages are skipped and the key is stored under a no-auth AES-GCM keystore key. The write succeeds, reads never prompt. `securityLevel: SECURE_HARDWARE` does not prevent this (it only validates TEE-backing). **2. The app lock has no authentication mechanism of its own.** `BiometricLockModal` "unlocks" by reading the stored private key via `getPrivateKey()`. Consequences: - Android (no biometrics): the auto-unlock keychain read succeeds instantly → lock dismisses itself, no gate at all. - Android (with biometrics): the keystore key accepts `AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG or AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` with a 5s validity window, and timeout-based keys are satisfied by the device unlock itself — reopening the app shortly after unlocking the phone typically passes with no prompt. - The lock is coupled to persisted keys, so it cannot survive the planned stateless-signing migration (see follow-up issue). ## Tasks ### Android storage fallback (lib/secureKeyStorage.ts) - [ ] In the biometric-protected writers (`storePrivateKey`, `storeNostrPrivateKey`, `storeAuthKey`): on Android, when `getSupportedBiometryType()` returns null, use `ACCESS_CONTROL.DEVICE_PASSCODE` instead of `BIOMETRY_CURRENT_SET` (maps to `usePasscode = true` → auth-requiring storage with device-credential prompt). - [ ] If the device has no lock screen at all (passcode storage also unavailable — library would silently fall through to no-auth again), throw instead of storing. ### Standalone app lock (components/BiometricLockModal.tsx) - [ ] Replace the `getPrivateKey()`-based unlock with `expo-local-authentication` `authenticateAsync({ disableDeviceFallback: true })` — biometric-only on both platforms (LAContext on iOS, BIOMETRIC_STRONG-only BiometricPrompt on Android), decoupled from key storage. - [ ] On devices without biometrics, fall back to a device-credential prompt (`disableDeviceFallback: false`), consistent with the storage fallback above. - [ ] New dependency: `expo-local-authentication`. ## Non-goals - No custom native module for true biometric-only keystore keys on Android (`setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)` + enrollment invalidation) — not worth hardening a storage layer slated for removal by stateless signing. - iOS broken-biometrics lockout flow (30s auto-logout + wipe) stays as is.
